Which order the three columns stand in. Anomaly Default is the game's own - the other party on the left, what you are wearing in the middle, your bag on the right. Tarkov-like puts the equipment against the left edge with your bag beside it. Everything else is the same either way; only the columns move.

Anything you pick up or loot goes into a container you are carrying that already holds one of the same thing - and a container can be dragged onto straight from a body's list. Only into a container that already has that kind in it: something already in there is you having said where it lives.

Plain olive webbing in an X across the back, three open-top pouches and a small admin pocket. What a rookie is handed and what a rookie makes do with. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

A slim dark-camo harness - a grenade pouch, a couple of pockets, and room for nothing you were not already carrying. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Flea-market patchwork: three mismatched pouches stitched onto a strap by somebody who was not paid much for it. Bandit kit, and it looks it. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Olive canvas with cross-stitched flaps and a zip pouch along the bottom. Old army issue, and still the honest choice. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Mercenary black nylon: four magazines standing up front, a flat admin pouch between two big flap-top pockets. Cut for NATO steel. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. An ecologist's frame - deep sample pockets, a radio lead over the shoulder and not one thing on it that rattles. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Duty issue. Plain, square, organised, and every pouch on it closes properly. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Army recon kit: a belt and a chest panel that work together, with the pouches cut deep enough to swallow a long stick. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Freedom's own, in faded green - loud patches, quiet buckles, and shingles down the front. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

A working rig: magazines standing proud, a sheathed knife, shears and a taped-up medical pouch. Half the Zone wears one. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

A radio and its aerial on one side, a row of shingles across the front, and bungee cord over all of it. A scout's rig, and silent with it. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Army heavy: a broad chest panel hung with dump bags, made for carrying more than you should have to. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

Mercenary black, cut long. The deepest shingles anyone sells, and nothing on it apologises for the weight. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

A carrier stripped back to its webbing - shell loops across the chest and a pouch on every panel. Assault kit, front to back. Right-click it into the rig slot at the top of the middle column. Anything that fits a slot goes in it - magazines, medicine, loose ammunition - and what is in the rig is what you can reach in a fight; the two slots beside it take expansion pouches.

A frosted plastic case with dark red latches and a winged shield stencilled across the lid. Watertight, and it does not care what the weather is doing to the outside of it. 5 by 5 squares inside, and it carries 10 kg. It takes medical supplies, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 99 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

Surplus olive drab steel with a webbing handle and a winged cartridge stencil on the side. Heavy empty. Heavier full. 4 by 2 squares inside, and it carries 10 kg. It takes ammunition, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 99 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

The same steel in a crate you need both hands for - four latches, a stencilled round on the lid and a wall of it inside. 6 by 4 squares inside, and it carries 15 kg. It takes ammunition, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 99 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A grey field cooler on a shoulder strap - black latches, knife and fork stencilled across the front, and enough insulation that what goes in cold comes out cold. 5 by 5 squares inside, and it carries 10 kg. It takes food, drink, cooked mutant meat and raw mutant meat, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 99 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A little wheeled cooler with a blue lid, knife and fork on the side. A day out rather than a week. 4 by 2 squares inside, and it carries 10 kg. It takes food, drink, cooked mutant meat and raw mutant meat, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 99 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A black composite case on heavy latches, with a stencilled figure in a suit across the lid. Deep enough to lay a plate carrier flat and stiff enough that nothing in it gets bent. 4 by 6 squares inside, and no weight limit at all - if it fits, it goes. It takes armour, helmets and masks, and chest rigs, and nothing else. Nothing stacks in it - one thing to a square. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

An olive crate with three magazines held under the lid by webbing straps. Everything stands upright and nothing rattles. 4 by 3 squares inside, and it carries 15 kg. It takes magazines, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 10 of them. Take a stack out and you get the fullest magazine in it; hold the split key instead and you get the emptiest. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A worn leather shoulder case with a single latch, the flap gone soft at the fold. Papers stand on edge inside it, so you read the names down the spines instead of turning out a pocketful of identical folded sheets. 1 by 24 squares inside, and no weight limit at all - if it fits, it goes. It takes documents, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, up to 20 of them. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A flat olive hard case with a winged crate stencilled on it. Foam inside, and it does not care whether what goes in it came off a rifle or off a suit. 4 by 5 squares inside, and it carries 15 kg. It takes weapon and armour parts, and nothing else. Identical things share a square, as many of them as the weight allows. Take a stack out and you get the least worn part in it; hold the split key instead and you get the most worn. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A hard olive case on twin latches, a rifle and wings stencilled across the lid. Foam cut to shape inside, so what goes in it comes out straight. Scopes, silencers and launchers are attachments and belong somewhere else. 6 by 3 squares inside, and no weight limit at all - if it fits, it goes. It takes weapons, and nothing else. Nothing stacks in it - one thing to a square. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.

A long olive rifle case, black caps on all four corners and a row of latches down the front, with the winged crest stencilled twice across the lid. Built to be thrown off a truck with something expensive inside it. Scopes, silencers and launchers are attachments and belong somewhere else. 8 by 4 squares inside, and no weight limit at all - if it fits, it goes. It takes weapons, and nothing else. Nothing stacks in it - one thing to a square. Right-click it to open it, then drag things in and out. It does not stack with another one - what is inside a box belongs to that box.
